body.x: Acetel (CEO Kang-hyeon Lee, www.acetel.co.kr) demonstrated an array of products from its media kit, including the Bluetooth remote-controlled selfie-stick, "Smart VJ Pole," at CES 2015, which will run Jan. 6-9 in Las Vegas.

The Smart VJ Pole is a Bluetooth remote control-activated selfie-stick designed for easy use. It was created to make picture and video capturing easier as the popularity of self-made video and media contents have risen in recent years.

The Bluetooth 4.0 remote control allows users to shoot from distances up to 30 meters away and comes with a remote control cap attached with a string for easy access. The Smart VJ Pole is built for durability and flexibility, and can be docked with a variety of devices up to 6 inches wide or DSLR cameras. The pole’s length can be stretched out at four different lengths from 29.5cm to 93cm.

"The ‘VJ Mount" is another flexible product and can be mounted to a wide array of equipment from camcorders to smartphones while the secure "VJ X-Grip" ensures recording on the go safely. These and other supplementary products such as the "VJ Twin Mount" will also be exhibited at CES 2015.

Regarding the upcoming exhibition, a spokesperson for Acetel shared, “We will show the high quality products of Korea to the global buyers at CES as we uncover new overseas partners in the self-smart media production market.”

Acetel has been involved in the digital broadcast solution industry for many years and has conducted joint ventures with a wide variety of companies. In recent years, it has built up a platform of smart media intended for video content production.

Held annually in January and owned and produced by the Consumer Electronics Association (CEA), CES 2015 is the world's largest IT and consumer electronics exhibition to see the latest global trends in consumer electronics industry in one spot.

Globally recognized for its record in the number of published articles for CES, AVING News has been sending its reporters to CES every year to deliver the fastest and freshest news on the spot. This year, AVING News is using smartphones for news reporting, in line with the trend of one-person media.
